mainTopic: ניסוך המים on סוכות: the משנה's procedure, the source for drawing the water, the stories of ששון, and the גמרא's explanations of the משנה
overview: This עמוד finishes the משנה about the ניסוך המים on סוכות. The two bowls on the מזבח had spouts of different widths, the water bowl was on the west and the wine bowl on the east, and switching them is still valid after the fact. רבי יהודה says the water was poured with a one-לוג vessel on all eight days. The pourer was told to raise his hand because a צדוקי once poured the water on his feet. On שבת the water was drawn on ערב שבת, and spilled or uncovered water was replaced from the כיור. The גמרא asks for the source of drawing the water, and רב עינא quotes "ושאבתם מים בששון". Two stories follow in which מינים named ששון, and then רבי אבהו, play on that פסוק. Next a ברייתא explains why the כהן turned left on the ramp, and the גמרא explains why even the water bowl turned black. It then proves that the משנה about the spouts follows the רבנן, not רבי יהודה. The עמוד ends with a ברייתא about the צדוקי who was pelted with אתרוגים and the damaged corner of the מזבח, which was sealed with salt.

steps.title: The two spouts of the silver bowls
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the two bowls on the מזבח. Each had a narrow spout, but the wine spout was wider than the water spout so both would finish pouring at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bowls had two thin nose-like spouts. One was wider and one was narrower, so that both would empty at the same moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is describing the two silver bowls used for the water and wine libations on top of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine is thicker than water and flows more slowly. So the wine bowl got a wider hole and the water bowl a narrower one. This way both libations finish together.

keyTerms.meaning: Nose-like spouts or openings at the bottom of the bowls
They finish at the same time

phrases.english: like two thin nose-shaped spouts,
one wide and one thin,
phrases.notes: The wide spout is for the wine and the thin spout is for the water.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם כָּלִין בְּבַת אַחַת.
phrases.english: so that both would finish at the same time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the two silver bowls, which began on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine spout was wider and the water spout narrower, so both libations would end at the same time.

steps.title: Which bowl is where, and what happens if they are switched
steps.stepSummary: The water bowl was on the west side and the wine bowl on the east side. If someone poured the water into the wine bowl, or the wine into the water bowl, he still fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The western bowl was for water and the eastern bowl was for wine. If he poured the water into the wine bowl, or the wine into the water bowl, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us where each bowl stood. It then rules that pouring into the wrong bowl is still valid after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The positions are the proper way to do it from the start (לכתחילה). But a mistake in placement does not ruin the libation after the fact (בדיעבד), so the person is יצא.

keyTerms.meaning: Its western one (the bowl on the west)
Its eastern one (the bowl on the east)
He poured (emptied one thing into another)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that the placement does not matter. It is the proper way to do it from the start. The משנה only says that switching them does not disqualify the libation after it already happened.

phrases.english: its western one — for water,
its eastern one — for wine.

phrases.aramaic: עֵירָה שֶׁל מַיִם לְתוֹךְ שֶׁל יַיִן,
phrases.english: If he poured the water one into the wine one,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל יַיִן לְתוֹךְ שֶׁל מַיִם — יָצָא.
phrases.english: or the wine one into the water one — he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the location of each bowl and a ruling for when they are mixed up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water goes in the west bowl and wine in the east bowl, but switching them is still valid after the fact.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: one לוג, all eight days
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the water was poured using a vessel holding one לוג. He also says it was done on all eight days, not only seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He would pour with a one-לוג vessel on all eight days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the earlier view in the משנה. He disagrees about the amount of water and about how many days the water was poured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view in the משנה held that the water was poured for seven days, using a three-לוג flask. רבי יהודה says the measure was one לוג. He also includes שמיני עצרת, which makes eight days.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of liquid volume; here, a vessel of that size
All eight days, including שמיני עצרת

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
with a log-vessel he would pour, all eight days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a dissenting תנא's view about the amount of water and the number of days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the water libation used one לוג and was done all eight days.

steps.title: "Raise your hand" and the story of the אתרוגים
steps.stepSummary: The one pouring was told to lift his hand so everyone could see the water go into the bowl. This was because a צדוקי once poured it on his feet, and the people pelted him with their אתרוגים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they say to the one pouring: "Raise your hand!" Because once, one man poured it on his feet, and all the people pelted him with their אתרוגים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a precaution for the pouring and tells the story behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקים did not accept the תורה שבעל פה, so they rejected the water libation. One צדוקי כהן deliberately poured the water on his feet instead of into the bowl. After that incident, the pouring was done with a raised hand so everyone could see it done properly.

keyTerms.meaning: They pelted him (threw things at him)

steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows how central the water libation was to the people. It also shows how publicly the תורה שבעל פה was defended against the צדוקים.

phrases.english: And to the one pouring, he says to him:
Raise your hand.
For once, one man poured
on his feet,
and all the people pelted him with their etrogim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a precaution for how the pouring is done, along with its historical reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one pouring must raise his hand so the water libation is clearly seen being done properly.

steps.title: How the water libation was done on שבת
steps.stepSummary: On שבת the ceremony was the same as on a weekday, with one difference. The water was drawn from the שילוח on ערב שבת into an unconsecrated golden barrel, which was kept in a chamber.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is done on a weekday, so it is done on שבת. The only difference is that on ערב שבת he would fill an unconsecrated golden barrel from the שילוח and leave it in the chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how the water libation works on שבת, when the water cannot be carried from the שילוח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying water from the שילוח on שבת would be forbidden. So the water was drawn the day before. The barrel was deliberately not consecrated, because consecrated vessels would sanctify the water overnight, and that water would then become פסול through לינה.

keyTerms.meaning: A chamber in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: As its performance on a weekday,
so is its performance on Shabbat,
except that he would fill on Shabbat eve
a golden barrel that was not consecrated
from the Siloam
and he would place it in the chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the weekday procedure to the special arrangement needed for שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת the water is drawn on ערב שבת into an unconsecrated golden barrel and kept in the chamber.

steps.title: Spilled or uncovered water is replaced from the כיור
steps.stepSummary: If the stored water spilled or was left uncovered, they drew water from the כיור instead. This is because uncovered wine or water is פסול for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it spilled or was left uncovered, he would fill from the כיור. For uncovered wine and water are unfit for the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה deals with a problem in the שבת arrangement: what to do if the stored water became unusable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquids left uncovered (גילוי) might have been poisoned by a snake, so a person may not drink them. Something unfit for a person to drink is also unfit for the מזבח. The backup source is the כיור, the washing basin in the Temple courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: The washing basin in the Temple courtyard
Unfit to be used on the altar

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with this rule: uncovered wine or water cannot be offered on the מזבח, so on שבת the backup water comes from the כיור.

phrases.english: If it spilled, or was uncovered,
he would fill from the basin.
For wine and water that are uncovered —
are unfit for the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׁפְּכָה, נִתְגַּלְּתָה, הָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִן הַכִּיּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Covers the case where the water prepared on ערב שבת became unusable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spilled or uncovered water is replaced with water from the כיור, because uncovered liquids are פסול for the מזבח.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking where these practices come from.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking for the source of the water-drawing ceremony described in the משנה. This question sets up the next step, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about how the water was drawn, as the משנה describes: from the spring of the שילוח, with ceremony and joy. It is not asking for the source of the water libation itself. A פסוק from נביאים, like the one in the next step, could not be the source of a תורה law.

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The textual source for the water-drawing ceremony.

steps.title: רב עינא cites the verse about drawing water with joy
steps.stepSummary: רב עינא answers with the פסוק from ישעיה: "You shall draw water with joy."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עינא said: Because the verse says, "And you shall draw water with joy..."
steps.whatsHappening: רב עינא answers the גמרא's question by quoting a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse speaks of drawing water from springs with joy. This connects to drawing water from the שילוח and to the great celebration that went along with it.
steps.confusionAlert: This פסוק is from ישעיה (12:3), not from the חומש. It serves here as the source for the ceremony and its joy.

phrases.english: Rav Eina said,
as the verse states:
"With joy you shall draw water, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ישעיה 12:3, "You shall draw water with joy from the springs of salvation."

steps.title: Two מינים named ששון and שמחה argue
steps.stepSummary: Two מינים, one named ששון and one named שמחה, argued over who was better. ששון claimed he was better because a פסוק lists ששון first.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were two מינים, one named ששון and one named שמחה. ששון said to שמחה: I am better than you, because it is written, "ששון and שמחה they shall obtain."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a side story connected to the word ששון in the פסוק it just quoted. ששון opens the argument by bragging that he comes first in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a word-play contest. Each person's name is a Hebrew word for joy. Whoever appears first in a פסוק claims to be more important.

keyTerms.meaning: Joy; here also a person's name
Happiness; here also a person's name

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a legal discussion. It is a short story that plays on the word ששון from the פסוק in step 8.

phrases.english: There were these two heretics,

phrases.aramaic: חַד שְׁמֵיהּ שָׂשׂוֹן וְחַד שְׁמֵיהּ שִׂמְחָה.
phrases.english: one was named Sason and one was named Simcha.
Sason said to Simcha:
I am better than you,
as it is written: "Sason and Simcha they shall obtain, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a story on the word ששון from the פסוק in step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ששון claims he is superior because he is listed first in a פסוק

steps.title: שמחה answers with a פסוק where he comes first
steps.stepSummary: שמחה pushes back. He quotes a פסוק from מגילת אסתר where שמחה comes before ששון.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמחה said to ששון: I am better than you, because it is written, "For the Jews there was שמחה and ששון."
steps.whatsHappening: שמחה answers ששון's boast. He uses the same kind of proof: a פסוק where his own name comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This cancels ששון's proof. Each name comes first in some פסוק, so word order proves nothing. The argument is now a tie.

keyTerms.meaning: For the Jews (a phrase from מגילת אסתר)

phrases.english: Simcha said to Sason:
I am better than you,
as it is written: "Simcha and Sason for the Jews."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שִׂמְחָה לְשָׂשׂוֹן: אֲנָא עֲדִיפְנָא מִינָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters ששון's proof with an opposite פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: ששון's claim that he comes first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק puts שמחה first, so word order proves nothing

steps.title: ששון mocks שמחה as a messenger
steps.stepSummary: ששון switches from bragging to insulting. He says שמחה will one day be sent out like an errand-runner, based on the words "בשמחה תצאו".
steps.simpleTranslation: ששון said to שמחה: One day they will dismiss you and make you a messenger, as it is written: "For with שמחה you shall go out."
steps.whatsHappening: ששון now mocks שמחה. He reads a פסוק as if people will "send out" שמחה, the way you send out a courier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תצאו ("you shall go out") is twisted to mean that שמחה is sent out. A פרוונקא is a lowly messenger who gets sent away on errands.

phrases.english: Sason said to Simcha:
One day they will dismiss you
and make you a messenger,
as it is written: "For with Simcha you shall go out."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the argument from "who is first" to personal insults
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reads "בשמחה תצאו" as שמחה being sent out like a lowly messenger

steps.title: שמחה mocks ששון as a water bucket
steps.stepSummary: שמחה hits back with our own פסוק, "ושאבתם מים בששון". He reads it as "you will draw water using ששון", as if ששון were a bucket.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמחה said to ששון: One day they will dismiss you and draw water with you, as it is written: "And you shall draw water with ששון."
steps.whatsHappening: שמחה gets the last word. He uses the very פסוק from step 8 to mock ששון as a tool for drawing water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter ב in בששון can mean "with" in the sense of "using". So שמחה reads the פסוק as people drawing water by using ששון as a container. This brings the story back to the פסוק of שמחת בית השואבה.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole story is a play on the ב of בששון. It can mean "with joy" or "using ששון" as a tool.

phrases.english: Simcha said to Sason:
One day they will dismiss you
and fill water with you,
as it is written: "And you shall draw water with Sason."

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד יוֹמָא שָׁבְקוּךְ וּמָלוּ בָּךְ מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ששון's insult with a sharper insult
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ששון will be used as a vessel to draw water, as in "ושאבתם מים בששון"

steps.title: A heretic named Sason boasts to רבי אבהו
steps.stepSummary: A different מין named ששון tells רבי אבהו that in עולם הבא the Jews will draw water for him. He bases this on "ושאבתם מים בששון".
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain מין named ששון said to רבי אבהו: You are destined to draw water for me in עולם הבא, as it is written: "And you shall draw water with ששון."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story about the same פסוק. Here a מין reads it as praising him. This sets up רבי אבהו's sharp reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מין treats the פסוק as a prediction about himself. He claims the Jews will serve him by drawing water for him.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from ארץ ישראל who often debated מינים

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא דִּשְׁמֵיהּ שָׂשׂוֹן
phrases.english: A certain heretic whose name was Sason said
to Rabbi Abahu:
You are destined to draw water for me
in the World to Come,
as it is written: "And you shall draw water with Sason."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא דִּשְׁמֵיהּ שָׂשׂוֹן לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story on the same פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מין claims the פסוק means the Jews will draw water for him

steps.title: רבי אבהו turns the verse against him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו points out that the פסוק says בששון ("with"), not לששון ("for"). So it means the man's skin will become a water bag.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it were written "לששון" (for ששון), it would be as you say. Now that it is written "בששון" (with ששון), the skin of that man will be made into a water bag, and we will fill water with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the מין by reading the exact letter in the פסוק. He shows that it actually insults the מין instead of praising him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter ל would mean the water is drawn for ששון. The letter ב means the water is drawn with ששון, as a tool. So the man himself, specifically his skin, becomes the container.

keyTerms.meaning: A leather bag for holding liquid (a flask)

steps.whatToRemember: ל means "for" and ב means "with/using". רבי אבהו wins by reading the exact letter in the פסוק.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If it were written "for Sason", it would be as you say;
now that it is written "with Sason",
the skin of that man
we will make into a water bag
and fill water with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מין's claim from step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בששון means "using ששון", so the מין's skin will become a water bag

steps.title: General rule: go up on the right, come down on the left
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: the כהן went up the ramp and turned left. A ברייתא explains that normally everyone going up to the מזבח turns right, circles around, and comes down on the left.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He went up the כבש and turned to his left, etc." The רבנן taught: All who go up to the מזבח go up by way of the right, circle around, and go down by way of the left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה. It brings a ברייתא with the normal rule for walking on the מזבח. This sets up the exception in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual path is to turn right, walk all the way around the top of the מזבח, and exit on the left. That makes the משנה's "turned left" stand out as unusual. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח

phrases.english: "He went up the ramp and turned to his left, etc."
The Rabbis taught:
All who go up to the altar
go up by way of the right and circle around
and go down by way of the left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories and returns to explaining the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Normally one goes up on the right, circles the מזבח, and comes down on the left

steps.title: Three exceptions where you turn left
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists three jobs where the כהן turns left and comes back the same way: ניסוך המים, ניסוך היין, and עולת העוף when the usual spot was crowded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for one going up for these three things, who goes up by way of the left and turns back on his heel. These are: the water libation, the wine libation, and the bird burnt-offering when there were many in the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by listing the exceptions to the normal right-side path. ניסוך המים, from our משנה, is one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For these jobs the כהן turns left and does not circle the מזבח. He does his task and turns around on his heel. This explains why the משנה says the כהן "turned to his left" for the water pouring.

keyTerms.meaning: Turn back on the heel (return the same way)
Pouring the water on the מזבח on סוכות
Pouring the wine on the מזבח
A bird brought as a burnt-offering

steps.whatToRemember: Turning left is the exception. It is used for ניסוך המים, ניסוך היין, and a crowded עולת העוף.

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִן הָעוֹלֶה לִשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ,
phrases.english: Except for one who goes up for these three things,
for they go up by way of the left
and turn back on their heel.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: נִיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם, וְנִיסּוּךְ הַיַּיִן,
phrases.english: And these are they: the water libation, and the wine libation,
and the bird burnt-offering when there were too many in the east.
phrases.notes: When the usual spot on the east side was crowded, the extra birds were done elsewhere

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּץ מִן הָעוֹלֶה לִשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the exceptions to the general rule in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For ניסוך המים, ניסוך היין, and a crowded עולת העוף, one goes up on the left and turns back

steps.title: Why would the water bowl turn black?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the bowls darkened. The גמרא accepts that wine would darken a bowl, but asks why the water bowl would darken.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Except that they would turn black." It makes sense that the wine bowl turns black. Why would the water bowl turn black?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's line in the משנה that the bowls darkened. It then challenges it: water should not stain anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said the bowls were plaster, not silver, and that they turned black. Wine can stain a bowl, but plain water should not. So why say both bowls darkened?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that... (sets up a contrast)

phrases.english: "Except that they would turn black."
phrases.notes: Quote from רבי יהודה in the משנה

phrases.english: It makes sense that the wine bowl turns black,
but why would the water bowl turn black?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּיַיִן מַשְׁחִיר, דְּמַיָּא אַמַּאי מַשְׁחִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that both bowls turned black
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water does not stain, so the water bowl should not darken

steps.title: Wine sometimes ends up in the water bowl
steps.stepSummary: The משנה itself says that if the כהן mixed up the bowls, he still fulfilled the מצוה. So wine sometimes got poured into the water bowl, and over time it turned black too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Master said: If he poured the water into the wine bowl, or the wine into the water bowl, he fulfilled his obligation. So the water bowl will also come to turn black.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to another rule in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mixing up the bowls was allowed after the fact, so wine sometimes went into the water bowl. That wine slowly stained the water bowl as well. The question is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: It will come to turn black

steps.whatToRemember: The water bowl darkened because wine was sometimes poured into it, and that was still valid.

phrases.english: Since the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: עֵירָה שֶׁל מַיִם לְתוֹךְ שֶׁל יַיִן,
phrases.english: If he poured the water into the wine bowl,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל יַיִן לְתוֹךְ שֶׁל מַיִם יָצָא —
phrases.english: or the wine into the water bowl, he fulfilled his obligation,
so the water bowl will also come to turn black.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uses another rule from the same משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only wine was ever in the wine bowl, and only water in the water bowl
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine sometimes went into the water bowl, which was valid, so that bowl darkened too

steps.title: Does the משנה follow only רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that the bowls had two nose-like holes, one wider and one thinner. It suggests this must follow רבי יהודה, who holds the water bowl was smaller (one לוג). According to the רבנן, both bowls were the same size, so why would the holes be different?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And the bowls had holes like two narrow noses, etc.' Shall we say that our משנה follows רבי יהודה and not the רבנן? For we learned that רבי יהודה says: He would pour the water with a one-לוג vessel on all eight days. Because if it followed the רבנן, the two bowls are the same size!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next piece of the משנה and suggests it fits only רבי יהודה's view, not the view of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says one bowl had a wider hole and one had a thinner hole. That makes sense if the bowls held different amounts, so that both would finish emptying at the same time. רבי יהודה holds the water was only one לוג, so the bowls held different amounts. The רבנן hold both held three לוגין, so different holes seem pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Having holes (the bowls had holes at the bottom)
Shall we say? (introduces a proposed conclusion)
They are the same as each other

phrases.english: And they had holes like two noses, etc.
Shall we say our Mishnah follows Rabbi Yehuda
and not the Rabbis,
as we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He would pour with a one-log vessel all eight days.
phrases.notes: The water was one לוג, smaller than the wine's three

phrases.english: For if it is the Rabbis, they are the same size!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא וְלָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה after the discussion of the darkened bowls
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's different-sized holes show that it follows רבי יהודה alone

steps.title: Wine is thick and water is thin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Even the רבנן need different holes, because wine is thick and flows slowly, while water is thin and flows fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the רבנן: wine is thick, and water is thin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion and shows the משנה can fit the רבנן too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if both bowls held the same amount, thick wine pours out more slowly than thin water. So the wine bowl needed a wider hole for both bowls to empty at the same time. The different holes therefore do not prove the bowls were different sizes.

phrases.english: You can even say it is the Rabbis:
Wine is thick, water is thin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה must follow רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The difference in thickness between wine and water explains the different holes, even when the bowls are the same size

steps.title: רבי יהודה describes the holes differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that it makes sense the משנה follows the רבנן. In a ברייתא, רבי יהודה describes the openings as 'wide' and 'narrow', a much bigger difference than the משנה describes. He needs that bigger difference because his bowls held different amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it is logical. For רבי יהודה holds 'wide' and 'narrow', as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says: There were two pipes there, one for water and one for wine. The wine pipe had a wide mouth, and the water pipe had a narrow mouth, so that both would finish at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings support for its answer: the משנה's wording does not match how רבי יהודה describes the openings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes a small difference between the holes, one slightly wider and one thinner. That fits the רבנן, who only need to make up for wine being thicker. רבי יהודה needs a big difference (wide versus narrow) because three לוגין of wine must empty in the same time as one לוג of water.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical (introduces support)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two descriptions. The משנה's version (slightly wider versus thinner) is a small difference. רבי יהודה's version (wide versus narrow) is a big one. The proof depends on that gap.

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
for if it were Rabbi Yehuda —
he holds 'wide' and 'narrow.'
As a baraita teaches: Rabbi Yehuda says:
There were two pipes there,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שֶׁל מַיִם וְאֶחָד שֶׁל יַיִן.
phrases.english: one for water and one for wine.
The wine one — its mouth was wide,
the water one — its mouth was narrow,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם כָּלִין בְּבַת אַחַת,
phrases.english: so that both would finish at the same time,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 20
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows the רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה describes the openings as wide and narrow, unlike the משנה's wording

steps.title: Conclusion: the משנה follows the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion by accepting the proof from step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה's wording does not match רבי יהודה's, the משנה follows the רבנן. This ends the first suggestion, that it follows רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: The difference in thickness between wine and water shows only that the משנה can follow the רבנן (step 20). The proof that it really does follow them comes from the wording. The משנה says מעובה and דק, while רבי יהודה says רחב and קצר (step 21).

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 21
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה follows the רבנן, not רבי יהודה

steps.title: The צדוקי who poured the water on his feet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about the water bowl on the west side. A ברייתא tells of a צדוקי כהן who poured the water on his feet instead of into the bowl, and all the people threw their אתרוגים at him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The western one was for water.' The רבנן taught: There was an incident with a certain צדוקי who poured the water on his feet, and all the people pelted him with their אתרוגים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא with a story that explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקים did not accept ניסוך המים, because it comes from the oral tradition rather than an explicit פסוק. So this כהן poured the water on his feet on purpose. This story is why the people would tell the כהן to raise his hand, so they could see him pour properly into the bowl.

keyTerms.meaning: A צדוקי, one who rejected the תורה שבעל פה

phrases.english: Its western one was for water.
The Rabbis taught:
There was an incident with a certain Sadducee
who poured the water on his feet,
and all the people pelted him with their etrogim.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲרָבוֹ שֶׁל מַיִם. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּצַדּוּקִי אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צדוקי כהן poured the water on his feet, and the people pelted him with אתרוגים

steps.title: The damaged altar corner sealed with salt
steps.stepSummary: That day a corner (קרן) of the מזבח was damaged. They sealed it with a lump of salt. This did not make the מזבח fit for the עבודה. It was only so that the מזבח would not be seen damaged.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that day the corner of the מזבח was damaged. They brought a lump of salt and sealed it. Not because this made it fit for the עבודה, but so that the מזבח would not be seen damaged.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the story by telling what happened to the מזבח and how they patched it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A damaged מזבח cannot be used for the עבודה, and a salt patch does not fix that. They sealed it anyway out of respect, so the מזבח would not look broken. The ברייתא makes clear the patch was for appearance only.

keyTerms.meaning: Became fit for the Temple service

steps.confusionAlert: The salt did NOT make the מזבח kosher for the עבודה. It only covered the damage so the מזבח would not look broken.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule of having the כהן raise his hand comes from this story of the צדוקי. The salt patch on the damaged מזבח was only out of respect, not to make it usable.

phrases.english: And that day the horn of the altar was damaged,
and they brought a lump of salt and sealed it.
Not because it became fit for the service,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא יֵרָאֶה מִזְבֵּחַ פָּגוּם.
phrases.english: but so that the altar would not be seen damaged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the ברייתא's story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The salt patch was only out of respect, so the מזבח would not look damaged. It did not make the מזבח fit for the עבודה.
